_doc: Bench for lint_paid_llm_entity.py. GUILT cases reach a paid per-token Anthropic endpoint; INNOCENCE cases do not. `missed_by_grep` marks the guilt cases today's catE-sovereignty-lint greps do NOT catch — that subset is the entire reason the lint exists, so its recall is the number that matters. PROVENANCE, because a corpus that hides who wrote it cannot be read: the first 19 guilt and 20 innocence cases were authored by the lane that wrote the judge, which said so plainly and named the honest next step as a refuter adding cases it thinks will fool it. On 2026-09-21 a session outside that lane added 7 guilt and 9 innocence cases, aimed at the two seams the independent bench run exposed: the route-by-PROCESS class (a shell or a raw HTTP request reaching the endpoint with no SDK and no wrapper — `shell_curl` scored 0.43 and `httpx_async_raw` 0.58, the only case in the empty band), and the FALSE-ALARM surface, which is the half that decides whether this step is safe to arm: a miss costs nothing under OR-composition, a false red costs a real author's PR. WHAT IS MEASURED ABOUT THE NEW CASES AND WHAT IS NOT: every one had its `missed_by_grep` value produced by running grep_verdict() rather than asserted, and every innocence case was checked not to fire the incumbent greps and to pass the prefilter so that it actually reaches the judge. Their MODEL verdicts are UNMEASURED — the refuter had no key, and adding cases does not re-run the bench. The recall and false-alarm figures quoted anywhere for this corpus describe the first 39 cases only until a bench run covers all 55.

class UpstreamAuth(httpx.Auth):
    def auth_flow(self, request):
        request.headers["x-api-key"] = os.environ["LLM_UPSTREAM_TOKEN"]
        request.headers["anthropic-version"] = "2023-06-01"
        yield request

           json={"model": "claude-sonnet-5", "max_tokens": 64, "messages": []})

innocence.name: docstring_explains_why_we_refuse
innocence.content:
"""Why this module builds no vendor SDK client.

CLAUDE.md bans reaching Claude through a paid per-token endpoint: the
subscription is already paid and a per-token credential duplicates it. The
sanctioned path is the claude CLI with its OAuth token, so that is all this
module does. Nothing here holds a vendor credential of any kind.
"""
import subprocess


def ask(prompt: str) -> str:
    out = subprocess.run(["claude", "-p", prompt], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.stdout
